_meta.indication: For patients 18 years of age or older who have limited or no alternative treatment options, for the treatment of complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI), including pyelonephritis caused by susceptible Gram-negative microorganisms

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, double-blind, parallel-group, randomized (2:1), active-controlled noninferiority trial comparing cefiderocol to imipenem/cilastatin (IMP)
pivotal_trials.population: Hospitalized adults 18 years and older with complicated urinary tract infection (cUTI) with or without pyelonephritis, or acute uncomplicated pyelonephritis, caused by Gram-negative pathogens
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Composite of clinical response and microbiological eradication at the test-of-cure (TOC) visit (7 ± 2 days after end of treatment) in the micro-ITT population
pivotal_trials.n: 452 subjects randomized; micro-ITT population had 252 in the cefiderocol group and 119 in the IMP group (analysis excluding 11 GCP-noncompliant subjects)
pivotal_trials.result: Composite success 183/252 (72.6%) with cefiderocol vs 65/119 (54.6%) with IMP; treatment difference 18.6% (95% CI 8.2% to 28.9%), meeting criteria for statistical superiority

key_safety: Most frequent adverse reactions (≥2%) were diarrhea (4%), infusion site reactions (4%), constipation (3%), rash (3%), candidiasis (2%), cough (2%), elevations in liver tests (2%), headache (2%), hypokalemia (2%), nausea (2%), and vomiting (2%). Serious adverse reactions occurred in 14/300 (4.7%) FETROJA patients; the most serious labeled risk is an increase in all-cause mortality in patients with carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative infections
target_moa: Cefiderocol is a cephalosporin whose catechol moiety acts as a siderophore, chelating iron and using the bacterial iron transport system to penetrate the outer membrane; it then binds penicillin-binding proteins and inhibits cell wall (peptidoglycan) synthesis, producing bactericidal activity against Gram-negative bacteria

boxed_warning.content: No boxed warning; the mortality signal from the CREDIBLE-CR trial was communicated as a Warning and Precaution (section 5.1) rather than a Boxed Warning

advisory_committee.vote: Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee met October 16, 2019; voted 14 Yes, 2 No, 0 Abstain that substantial evidence of efficacy and sufficient evidence of safety was provided for the cUTI indication

description.text: Added indication for treatment of Hospital-acquired/Ventilator-associated Bacterial Pneumonia (HABP/VABP) in adults 18 years and older

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for the use of FETROJA in patients 18 years of age and older for the treatment of Hospital-acquired Bacterial Pneumonia and Ventilator-associated Bacterial Pneumonia (HABP/VABP) caused by the following susceptible Gram-negative microorganisms: *Acinetobacter baumannii* complex, *Escherichia coli*, *Enterobacter cloacae* complex, *Klebsiella pneumoniae*, *Pseudomonas aeruginosa*, and *Serratia marcescens*.

summary.text: Cefiderocol received QIDP and fast track designations on August 18, 2015, and NDA 209445 was submitted December 14, 2018 with priority review; the goal date was extended three months for a major amendment, an Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee (October 16, 2019) voted 14 to 2 in favor, and the traditional approval was based on the single Phase 2 APEKS-cUTI trial.

citations.quote: Cefiderocol was granted both fast track and Qualified Infectious Disease Product designation on August 18, 2015, for the following indications: cUTI, hospital acquired bacterial pneumonia (HABP), ventilator associated bacterial pneumonia (VABP), and bloodstream infections (bacteremia).
December 14, 2018: NDA 209445 submitted to the Agency with priority review status.
The pivotal evidence of effectiveness of cefiderocol in patients with cUTI including pyelonephritis with limited or no alternative treatment was provided by one Phase 2 study (APEKS-cUTI Study).
